text: The dual coaction is determined by contracting against m: its coefficient is S((φ⊗id)ρ(m)), matching the right-comodule dual of [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). Finite projectivity makes the tensor–Hom comparison invertible, so this equation uniquely defines a tensor without choosing a basis. The construction uses S, not an assumed inverse of S. Checks pass: [dualTensorHom_dualCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L74), [dualCoact_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L83).
The defining contraction equals the antipode of the matrix coefficient.
Finite-basis calibration of the basis-free construction.

Contracting the dual coaction converts it into the linear map m↦S(c(φ,m)), where c(φ,m)=(φ⊗id)ρ(m). This is exactly the coefficient equation of [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). The equality is between linear maps in m; finite projectivity is what makes contraction identify tensors with all such maps. Checks pass: [dualTensorHom_dualCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L74), [dualCoact_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L83).
Pointwise characteristic equation.
The characteristic equation recovers the dual-basis sum.

Evaluating the contracted dual coaction at m gives the antipode of the original coefficient c(φ,m), as in [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). The notation abbreviates a finite tensor sum, not a chosen matrix entry or basis. Its order is that of a right coaction, and no commutativity of H is assumed. Checks pass: [dualCoact_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L83), [baseChangeEvaluation_dual_endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Evaluation.lean#L118).
Explicit formula in a finite basis.
Coefficient equation gives inverse-point evaluation on pure tensors.

Applying the counit to the coefficient of the dual coaction returns φ⊗1, hence φ after identifying M*⊗R with M*. This verifies counitality for the dual of [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47): the antipode preserves the counit, and the counit of c(φ,m) is φ(m). The displayed flipped tensor map simply inserts 1. Checks pass: [dualTensorHom_dualCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L74), [counit_matrixCoefficient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MatrixCoefficient/Basic.lean#L160).
The dual coefficient is the antipode of the original coefficient.
Counit of the original coefficient recovers evaluation.

The dual coaction satisfies right coassociativity because the antipode reverses coproduct factors, precisely the duality mechanism in [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). Contraction against every vector reduces the tensor identity to the original coaction law. Finite projectivity makes contraction injective; neither cocommutativity nor bijectivity of the antipode is needed. Checks pass: [dualCoact_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L83), [dual_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L211).
Finite-basis dual coaction formula.
The selected dual structure uses this coaction.

This equips the linear dual of a finite projective comodule with its antipode-twisted right coaction, the construction of [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). The counit and coassociativity laws are supplied explicitly. It is a selected structure rather than a global instance, and its existence does not assert that the antipode is invertible. Checks pass: [dualCoact_counit](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L95), [dualCoact_coassoc](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L157).
Dual counitality.
Dual coassociativity.

The explicitly selected dual comodule uses exactly dualCoact, characterized by the antipode-twisted coefficient equation in [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). Thus the structure introduces no alternative coaction on the same linear dual. The finite-projective hypotheses belong to this construction; the notation coact suppresses the locally selected dual instance in the displayed equation. Checks pass: [dualTensorHom_dualCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L74), [dualCoact_eq_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L83).
Characteristic equation identifies the chosen dual coaction.
Its finite-basis expression.

Pairing a⊗φ with the point action on b⊗m gives ab times the point evaluated at c(φ,m). This is the coefficient-evaluation dictionary of [Milne, Remark 4.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), with both scalar factors retained. The statement only needs a coalgebra and an algebra-valued point; it requires neither finite projectivity nor an antipode. Checks pass: [baseChangeEvaluation_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Dual/BaseChange.lean#L68), [endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L119).
The underlying scalar-extended pairing has factors a and b.
The point action evaluates the coefficient of the original coaction.

Evaluating the transformed dual functional on a pure vector gives ab·g⁻¹(c(φ,m)), implementing the inverse in the contragredient formula of [Milne, contragredient formula, p.472](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=483). WithConv means convolution of algebra-valued points, so this inverse is composition with the antipode, not pointwise reciprocal of values. The value algebra is commutative; H need not be. Checks pass: [dualTensorHom_dualCoact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Dual.lean#L74), [baseChangeEvaluation_dual_endOfPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Evaluation.lean#L134).
The dual coefficient applies the antipode.
The pure-tensor formula extends to arbitrary tensors.

The dual point action is adjoint to the inverse original action: ⟨gξ,z⟩=⟨ξ,g⁻¹z⟩, the contragredient rule of [Milne, contragredient formula, p.472](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=483). Bilinearity extends the pure-tensor calculation to arbitrary scalar-extended arguments. The pairing is canonical evaluation, not an inner product, and no identification of arbitrary infinite duals after scalar extension is used. Checks pass: [baseChangeEvaluation_dual_endOfPoint_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Evaluation.lean#L118), [baseChangeEvaluation_dual_endOfPoint_invariant](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Evaluation.lean#L152).
Pure-tensor inverse-point calibration.
Acting on both arguments preserves the pairing.

Acting by the same point on a finite-projective comodule and its dual preserves their scalar-extended evaluation pairing. The inverse in the contragredient formula of [Milne, contragredient formula, p.472](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=483) cancels the action on the vector argument. This is bilinear evaluation invariance, without a norm, positivity, complex conjugation or an assumption that H is commutative. Checks pass: [baseChangeEvaluation_dual_endOfPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Evaluation.lean#L134), [endOfPoint_inv_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L519).
Adjointness uses the inverse point.
The inverse-point action cancels the original action.

The linear-map space receives the coaction transported from M*⊗N under φ⊗n↦(m↦φ(m)n). Finite projectivity of M makes this identification invertible; N is arbitrary. The dual factor follows [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). Its position matters for noncommutative H: this declaration does not identify the coaction with the reversed tensor order. Checks pass: [linearHom_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L71), [baseChangeTensorHom_endOfPoint_linearHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L81).
Explicit transported coaction formula.
On commutative-valued points the action is target action followed by inverse source action.

After the canonical scalar-extension comparison, a point acts on a linear map by g_N∘f∘g_M⁻¹. The inverse source factor comes from the dual action in [Milne, contragredient formula, p.472](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=483); the target factor comes from the tensor action. Finite projectivity is assumed only for M, while commutativity of the value algebra permits scalar coefficients to commute. Checks pass: [linearHom_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L71), [baseChangeEvaluation_dual_endOfPoint](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Evaluation.lean#L134).
The Hom coaction comes from the ordered tensor M*⊗N.
The dual factor evaluates against the inverse original action.

The scalar extension of f is fixed by a specified point exactly when it intertwines that point’s actions on M and N. This follows by cancelling the inverse source action in the contragredient rule of [Milne, contragredient formula, p.472](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=483). It concerns this point alone; being a comodule morphism requires the universal coaction equation. Checks pass: [baseChangeTensorHom_endOfPoint_linearHom](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L81), [endOfPoint_comp_inv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/PointsAction.lean#L525).
Conjugation formula for the Hom point action.
The source action has the required inverse.

A comodule morphism f:N→P acts on linear-map comodules by postcomposition q↦f∘q. Tensoring f with the identity on the dual and transporting gives precisely this compatible map, using the dual of [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). M must be finite projective to form these Hom comodules; neither target needs projectivity. Checks pass: [linearHomPostcomp_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L170), [linearHomPostcomp_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L197).
Underlying action is ordinary postcomposition.
Postcomposition respects composition of comodule morphisms.

Forgetting coaction compatibility leaves the ordinary linear operator q↦f∘q. This confirms that tensoring the target map and transporting through M*⊗N changes no underlying function, with the dual convention of [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). The name compRight refers to inserting q on the right of f, rather than precomposing q by f. Checks pass: [linearHomPostcomp_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L170), [linearHomPostcomp_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L186).
Elementwise postcomposition formula.
Postcomposition by the identity is the identity.

The induced morphism of Hom comodules sends q exactly to f∘q, so evaluation at m is f(q(m)). This makes the construction from the dual tensor factor of [EGNO, Remark 1.22.7](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47) concrete. Coaction compatibility is additional structure on this familiar linear operator; it does not change the order of composition. Checks pass: [linearHomPostcomp_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L160), [linearHomPostcomp_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L197).
Underlying operator is ordinary postcomposition.
Composition order agrees with the bundled construction.

A surjection f:N→P induces a surjection Hom_R(M,N)→Hom_R(M,P) because M is projective, matching [Stacks, §10.77](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05CD). Finite generation is retained for the surrounding comodule construction. The lifted elements are ordinary linear maps; this theorem does not assert surjectivity on invariant vectors or an equivariant lift of every comodule morphism. Checks pass: [linearHomPostcomp_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L170), [linearHomPostcomp_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L186).
The map being proved surjective is exactly q↦f∘q.
Identity postcomposition gives the expected trivial surjection.

For commutative H, a linear map is invariant in the Hom comodule exactly when it intertwines the coactions. The proof uses the universal H-valued point, as in [Milne, Proposition 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107), so nonreduced coefficients are included. Commutativity is essential here: the general Hom construction alone does not imply this fixed-morphism characterization. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_linearHom_one_tmul_eq_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L129), [fixedLinearHomEquiv_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L259).
Fixed-point condition becomes intertwining of point actions.
The resulting invariant-to-morphism correspondence retains the same linear map.

This linear equivalence identifies invariant vectors in Hom_R(M,N) with comodule morphisms M→N by keeping the underlying linear map. The universal-point criterion of [Milne, Proposition 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107) supplies exactly its compatibility proof. The source M is finite projective and H is commutative; the equivalence does not follow from invariance under field-valued points alone. Checks pass: [fixedLinearHomEquiv_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L259), [fixedLinearHomEquiv_symm_coe](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L265).
Forward equivalence preserves the underlying linear map.
Inverse equivalence preserves the underlying linear map.

The invariant-to-morphism equivalence returns the original linear map after forgetting its compatibility proof. This is the concrete correspondence furnished by the coaction criterion in [Milne, Proposition 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107). Invariance is therefore used to certify equivariance, not to average or alter the map; commutative H and a finite-projective source remain the relevant hypotheses. Checks pass: [mem_fixedSubcomodule_linearHom_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L214), [fixedLinearHomEquiv_symm_coe](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L265).
The invariant condition is exactly the required coaction compatibility.
The inverse also retains the same map.

The inverse equivalence sends a comodule morphism to its underlying linear map regarded as an invariant vector in Hom_R(M,N). This implements the universal coaction criterion of [Milne, Proposition 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107) without modifying that map. The equality concerns the underlying function; the invariant membership proof is supplied by equivariance and the commutative-coefficient hypothesis. Checks pass: [fixedLinearHomEquiv_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L259), [mem_fixedSubcomodule_linearHom_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L214).
The forward map likewise retains the underlying linear map.
Equivariance supplies invariant membership.

Surjectivity of postcomposition on invariant Hom vectors lets the invariant identity of M lift to a comodule section s, with f∘s=id_M. The identification of invariants uses [Milne, Proposition 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107). Surjectivity on invariants is an explicit stronger hypothesis than ordinary surjectivity of f; finite projectivity is required of M, not N. Checks pass: [fixedLinearHomEquiv_symm_coe](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L265), [linearHomPostcomp_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L170).
The identity morphism gives the same identity as an invariant Hom vector.
A lifted invariant satisfies the desired right-inverse equation.

This is the submodule defined by ρ(m)=m⊗1; each such tensor already lies in its tensor image, proving stability. For affine-group comodules this is precisely [Milne, Proposition 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107), including all algebra-valued points. The definition also permits a coalgebra with a distinguished element called 1, without assuming that element is grouplike. Checks pass: [mem_fixedSubcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L75), [fixedSubcomodule_eq_top_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L81).
Membership is exactly the stated coaction equation.
All vectors are invariant exactly when the coaction is everywhere m↦m⊗1.

A comodule morphism restricts to a linear map on the vectors satisfying ρ(m)=m⊗1, since its intertwining equation preserves that condition. For affine groups these are the invariants of [Milne, Proposition 4.33](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=107). The restricted map keeps the original function; no averaging, flatness or assertion of surjectivity on invariants is part of the construction. Checks pass: [fixedMap_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L105), [fixedMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L118).
The restriction acts by the original morphism.
Restriction to invariant vectors respects composition.

Every extended nonnegative value equals the sum of its two halves, including zero and infinity. For infinity, division by the finite positive number two still gives infinity, and ∞+∞=∞. Thus the identity remains valid at the endpoint; it does not assert that each half is strictly smaller than the original value. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L540).

Half of a nonzero extended nonnegative value is strictly positive. No finiteness assumption is needed: half of infinity is infinity, which is positive in the extended order. The excluded input zero has half zero. Positivity of the half should not be confused with being strictly smaller than the original value. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L567).

Adding two strict inequalities preserves strict inequality in the extended nonnegative reals: a<c and b<d imply a+b<c+d. Both lower values are necessarily finite, while either upper value may be infinity. Requiring strictness in both hypotheses avoids the failure caused by adding a common infinite summand to one strict inequality. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L247).

Adding a fixed extended nonnegative value commutes with taking the infimum of any family. The family may be empty: its infimum is infinity, and both sides remain infinity. The fixed value may also be infinity, making both sides infinity. For finite values this is the usual translation rule for greatest lower bounds. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L546).

Cross multiplication gives c<a/b exactly when c·b<a, provided the denominator/comparison pair (b,c) is neither (0,∞) nor (∞,0). Positive finite denominators automatically satisfy these conditions. The exclusions reflect Lean’s endpoint conventions: in either excluded pair, c·b=0, while the strict quotient comparison is false, so equivalence can fail. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L389).

If b is positive and finite, the equality a·b=b holds exactly when a=1. The multiplier a may initially be any extended nonnegative value. Both restrictions on b matter: with b=0 every a satisfies the equality, and with b=∞ every positive a does, so neither endpoint determines a uniquely. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L94).

Multiplication by a positive finite value commutes with arbitrary infima of extended nonnegative values, including empty families. The empty infimum is infinity, so excluding a zero multiplier matters. An infinite multiplier can also fail: positive values tending to zero have infimum zero, but multiplying each by infinity makes their infimum infinity. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 5.4](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L866).

From a<b/c one may conclude a·c<b for extended nonnegative values without separate denominator restrictions. An infinite denominator makes the premise impossible because b/∞=0. A zero denominator can satisfy the premise when b>0; then a is finite and a·0=0<b. This is a one-way implication, not unrestricted cross-multiplication equivalence. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Inv.lean#L425).

Raising extended nonnegative values to the same natural-number power preserves non-strict inequalities. The exponent may be zero, when both powers are one, including 0⁰ and ∞⁰. Positive powers of infinity remain infinity. The statement concerns natural exponents and weak order; it does not claim strict preservation for exponent zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L49).

Every natural-number power of a finite extended nonnegative value is finite. Zero bases and zero exponents are included, using 0⁰=1. Finiteness of the base is sufficient, not necessary for an individual power: an infinite base also has finite zeroth power, since ∞⁰=1, although its positive powers are infinite. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.6](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Operations.lean#L242).

Converting a real number to [0,∞] gives a strictly positive value exactly when the original real is positive. Conversion first replaces negative inputs by zero, so every nonpositive real fails the positivity test. Positive inputs retain their ordinary values; no extra sign hypothesis is needed because the theorem states the exact equivalence. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L176).

When the upper real value q is strictly positive, comparison after conversion to [0,∞] is exact: converting p gives less than converting q precisely when p<q. The lower input p may be negative. Positivity of q prevents clipping from destroying strict comparison, as happens for −2<−1 when both conversions are zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L167).

For a nonnegative real a and a finite extended value b, converting a gives a value below b exactly when a is below b’s real value. Both guards matter: negative a can be clipped to zero, and infinity converts back to zero. Either change can invalidate the strict comparison outside the stated domain. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L267).

A nonpositive real number converts to zero in the extended nonnegative reals. This includes negative inputs, rather than embedding their signed values: the conversion takes max(p,0) before inclusion in [0,∞]. The declaration is the implication from the corresponding zero-value equivalence, so it assumes nonpositivity rather than concluding the original number is zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L196).

If an extended nonnegative value lies below the conversion of a nonnegative real b, its real value is at most b. The bound already forces the extended value to be finite. Nonnegativity of b is necessary here: with b negative and the extended value zero, the converted bound holds but the real comparison fails. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L283).

If an extended nonnegative value is strictly below the conversion of a real b, its real value is strictly below b. No separate sign or finiteness hypotheses are needed: the strict premise forces b positive and the extended value finite. For b≤0 the conversion is zero, so the premise cannot hold. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L293).

A strict inequality a<b between extended nonnegative values remains strict after conversion to reals when b is finite. The inequality itself then makes a finite, so only the upper value needs an explicit restriction. Without it, 1<∞ would become 1<0 because this conversion assigns zero to infinity. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Real.lean#L82).

An extended nonnegative value a is at most b if it is at most b+ε for every positive finite ε whenever b is finite. This is the usual arbitrarily small error criterion. If b is infinity, the conclusion holds automatically and the hypothesis imposes no restriction; otherwise density rules out a positive gap. Compared with [Faris §§2.5–2.7](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L614).

Converting any extended nonnegative value to a real always gives a nonnegative real. Finite values keep their usual nonnegative values, while infinity is assigned zero. This theorem asserts only the sign of the output: it does not say that the conversion preserves positivity, since infinity is positive but its converted value is zero. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L277).

Converting any real number to an extended nonnegative real always produces a finite value. A positive real keeps its value; zero and negative reals produce zero after clipping. Thus this conversion never reaches infinity, even though infinity belongs to its target type. The result places no sign restriction on the real input. Compared with [Faris §§2.6, 8.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L347).

An exact structure specifies the admissible short exact sequences in an additive category. Its idempotent completion formally adds images of projections e²=e. The new admissible sequences are precisely direct summands of the original ones, with splitting maps commuting with both sequence maps. The construction supplies the actual kernel, cokernel, pushout and pullback properties required for an exact category. See [Bühler, §6.3 and Proposition6.13](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0811.1480). Native Checks pass: [Compatible retracts of admissible sequences](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/Karoubi.lean#L296), [Admissible maps are arrow retracts](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/Karoubi.lean#L303), [The original embedding preserves exactness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/Karoubi.lean#L317).

For any nonnegatively graded commutative ring A and integer n, sections are locally homogeneous fractions r/s with deg(r)=deg(s)+n, interpreted in each prime localization. This is the shift A(n) followed by its associated sheaf on Proj A. The degree equation uses integers, including negative n; denominators are invertible locally. No generation in degree one or invertibility of O(n) is assumed. See [Stacks, Definition27.10.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01MM). Native Checks pass: [Every standard-open section is a homogeneous fraction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/TwistingSheaf/BasicOpen.lean#L93), [Vanishing is detected by annihilation by a power](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/TwistingSheaf/BasicOpen.lean#L65), [The degree-zero comparison is the canonical one](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/TwistingSheaf/Basic.lean#L524).

For any scheme map q:T→X and finite locally free sheaf E, maps over X into Spec_X(Sym E∨) correspond to global sections of q*E. The inverse evaluates dual linear coordinates at the section. Finite local freeness makes duality commute with arbitrary pullback; q need not be flat. Using E∨ makes the resulting points sections of E. See [Stacks, §27.4](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01LQ) and [§27.6, applied to E∨](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01M1). Native Checks pass: [The inverse is evaluation at the section](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/VectorBundle/TotalSpace.lean#L128), [Bundle maps act by their pulled-back linear map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/VectorBundle/TotalSpace.lean#L145). Free-coordinate calibration: [dual-basis evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/TensorProduct/Dual.lean#L159) and [off-diagonal zero](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/TensorProduct/Dual.lean#L175) are proved for every finite free family.
